claims: What makes personal 'Jarvis' agents work well is mostly the custom-instruction file derived from your chat history, not the hardware
A small model should tag every conversation with what the AI got wrong and how you like to use it; the main agent then returns new custom instructions
Most people do not need to build a Jarvis; set up custom instructions this way and 'your AI is gonna run so much better'
Article: 'AGI is here and 99% of people have no clue' (quoted founder)
how_to_steps: Export all AI data: ChatGPT Settings -> Data controls -> Export (gets conversations.json); do the equivalent in Claude
Install Jev into Claude Code: get key at console.typesafe.ai, run 'uvx jev-mcp-server install claude-code', restart the client

Feed the export to your agent; have Jev (jev_classify, model jev-latest) tag each chat as got_it_right / got_it_wrong and tag usage style (e.g. 'way too long', 'too verbose', 'no, it was Argentina'); output e.g. corrections.csv

Bring the analysis back to the main agent with the prompt: 'This is my whole ChatGPT history. Reverse engineer the custom instructions that turn you into my Jarvis. 1. Pull every time I corrected you... Misses are what to stop. 2. Keep patterns that show up... 3. Find the version of you that... 4. Write it as latent space... who it is, who I am... 5. Turn each correction into a rule... that generalizes. 6. Paste my own words as a voice... 7. Add a silent check... 8. Under 1,500 characters. A ChatGPT ... version.'
Paste the result into custom instructions (or CLAUDE.md)
on_screen_only: Title card 'There was never a Jarvis'; mind-map with nodes Finances, Clients, Sales, Communications, Marketing/Growth

relevance.why: Mining your own correction history into a CLAUDE.md / custom-instructions file is a sound, cheap personalization move for a founder who lives in Claude; Jev is optional, any cheap model can do the tagging.

implement_score.why: Half a day: export Claude/ChatGPT data, run Claude Code with Haiku over conversations.json to extract corrections and preferences, then generate a <1,500-char instruction block. Skip the Jev MCP unless its pricing/accuracy checks out.
